risks.note: Exports are 53% of total turnover across 13 countries, so the earnings base sits on a cycle the Company does not control. The FY27 case rests on a hoped-for 8-10% Class 8 recovery.

currentContext.expansion: The principal expansion event of FY2025-26 was the commencement of full-fledged operations at the Company's new smart mega die-casting plant at Thervoy Kandigai, Chennai, Tamil Nadu. The plant caters to growing demand for reliable, high-quality aluminium die-cast components across powertrain, structural, chassis and lightweighting applications, and is built on lean, green and connected principles - advanced robotic manufacturing cells, automated storage and retrieval systems (ASRS), autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) and a fully digital manufacturing ecosystem. A private 5G network deployed at the Thervoy Kandigai mega site supports scalable Industry 4.0 and IoT implementations, connected CCTV surveillance and Building Management System operations. The site is expected to meet more than 90% of its total energy needs through renewable sources. Footprint moved the other way as well: the Company divested the high-pressure and low-pressure aluminium die-casting businesses at its Hosur, Tamil Nadu plant on a slump-sale basis as a going concern to Sandhar Ascast Private Limited (a wholly owned subsidiary of Sandhar Technologies Limited), under a Business Transfer Agreement executed on 26th March 2025 following in-principle Board approval on 19th February 2025; the aggregate consideration was Rs 163 crore received in tranches, with the balance received during FY2025-26 and the proceeds used to reduce debt. Management states it adds capacity as required, in existing and new locations, to meet projected customer demand, closely monitoring customer projects and volumes to protect against both underutilisation and capacity shortages. Capacity-adjacent build-out also includes plant consolidation for manufacturing synergies, scale-up of Industry 4.0 connected-machine projects across manufacturing locations, and global R&D centres at Stuttgart, Germany and the IIT Research Park, Chennai. A US manufacturing facility is already in place, cited as the hedge against OEM localisation of sourcing. No rupee capex quantum, project cost or commissioning schedule for any future project is stated in the routed text.

Permanent worker turnover rose to 12.30% in FY2025-26 from 0.60% in FY2024-25 (3.81% in FY2023-24), with permanent employee turnover at 11.6% versus 14.47% the prior year - a structural people risk for a plant-consolidation and new-site-ramp year, though the figures also reflect the two-wheeler exit and Hosur divestment.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Management names it explicitly: 'Significant unfavorable movement in prices of fuel, logistics and key raw material, aluminium in global markets is one key factor that can affect the profit margins of the Company.' Middle East tensions are said to drive volatility in availability and prices across oil, freight and commodities. Partly mitigated because supply contracts provide for periodic price adjustments indexed to domestic and international aluminium prices, plus VA/VE cost reduction; but the pass-through is periodic, not immediate.
- Exports are 53% of total turnover across 13 countries, so the earnings base sits on a cycle the Company does not control. FY2025-26 showed how sharp that cycle is: North America Class 8 truck sales fell 20% and Class 5-7 fell 16% on tariff policy uncertainty, EPA emission-norm caution, high interest rates and freight weakness, while EU heavy trucks (>16T) grew only 1%. The FY27 case rests on a hoped-for 8-10% Class 8 recovery.
- The Directors' Report states the Company delivered FY26 'despite prolonged adverse global macroeconomic conditions and supply chain disruptions arising from U.S. tariff impacts.' The MD&A flags elevated global risk from geopolitical tensions, evolving trade policies and tariffs, and policy uncertainty across key economies, and says easing of the Middle East conflict is key for recovery in the second half of FY27.
- 100% of turnover comes from one activity - aluminium alloy cast articles including parts and components (NIC 24320) - sold to automotive OEMs and Tier-1 manufacturers. After the March 2025 exit of the two-wheeler business and the divestment of the Hosur as-cast undertaking, the revenue base is narrower still, concentrated in machined components for commercial vehicles and passenger vehicles, with no diversifying segment to offset an auto downturn.
- 'With significant exports, import of raw materials and capital goods, the Company is always exposed to impact on account of currency fluctuations.' Mitigation is a stated forex hedging policy, but the underlying two-sided exposure is structural given the export share and imported inputs and capital goods.
- 'Several Indian die casting companies and OEMs have set up or have been setting up new capacities over the past few years.' Management states that intense competition 'makes it extremely difficult to seek price increases to compensate the effects of inflation bringing the margins under severe pressure' - a direct threat to the FY26 EBITDA improvement to 17.2% from 12.6%.
- The Company adds capacity in existing and new locations against projected customer demand and has just commissioned the Thervoy Kandigai mega plant, so fixed cost and depreciation are committed ahead of volumes. Management says it closely monitors customer projects and volumes to protect from both underutilization and capacity shortages, and must keep securing new business 'to ensure better utilization of assets despite the increased competition and cost.'
- Stringent emission norms, fuel-economy regulation and adoption of alternate drivetrain technologies continue to reshape industry dynamics. OEMs estimating carbon footprint at every leg of the supply chain 'would eventually reorganize their global purchasing strategies, which could result in a strong push for localization' - a threat management says is mitigated by the existing US manufacturing facility, but one that keeps sourcing decisions outside the Company's control.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
